title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer thresholds to avoid regional thrashing during failovers
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: During a regional outage on 2026-02-19 we observed oscillation/"thundering" failovers where the SLO enforcer and circuit-breaker systems reopened capacity in the failing region too quickly, triggering load-shedding and immediate re-failover. This caused increased p95 latency spikes and customer errors. This hotfix tightens thresholds and adds a minimum stable window to prevent rapid reopen/close cycles across regions.

What this PR changes (summary):
- Add per-region min_stable_duration (configurable) in the SLO enforcer to require a region to be healthy for N seconds before reinstating routing weight. Default set to 30s.
- Smooth SLO breach rate using an exponential moving average (alpha=0.2) to avoid reacting to single-sample spikes.
- Adjust circuit breaker reopen backoff to increase on repeated flaps (exponential backoff with cap).
- Improve ordering in regional failover decision so that primary->secondary promotion considers in-flight KV-cache drain time to avoid request loss during rapid transitions.
- Add unit + integration tests for regional failover ordering and hysteresis behavior.

Files changed (high level):
- services/slo-enforcer/enforcer.go: add minStableDuration, EMA smoothing and tests.
- services/slo-enforcer/config.go: default config update and documentation.
- runtime/circuit_breaker/circuit_breaker.go: exponential backoff on reopen, add metrics for flap_count.
- routing/region_failover/manager.go: order/promote logic updated to consider kv_cache_drain_ms.
- tests/slo-enforcer/region_hysteresis_test.go: new integration test simulating failover thrash.
- docs/ops/slo-enforcer.md: updated rollout notes and emergency rollback steps.

Commits (high level):
- a1b2c3d: hotfix(slo-enforcer): add per-region min_stable_duration and EMA smoothing
- b2c3d4e: fix(circuit-breaker): exponential reopen backoff + flap_count metric
- c3d4e5f: test: add region_hysteresis integration test and CI harness adjustments
- d4e5f6a: docs: rollout notes and rollback plan for SLO enforcer flags

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added cover EMA smoothing and backoff logic.
- Integration test simulates region latency spike and verifies no reopen until min_stable_duration elapses.
- Ran full CI on main and a targeted staging canary for 2 hours against replayed traffic; observed stable routing with no thrash.
- Performance: added a micro-benchmark for the enforcer path; no measurable CPU regression in the hot path.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main (this PR).
2) Deploy to canary cluster (us-east-1) with feature flag slo_enforcer.hysteresis.enabled=true and min_stable_duration=30s for 2 hours.
3) If canary is healthy, roll to all regions over 30m with monitoring (SLO breach rate, flap_count metric).
4) If any unexpected regressions, flip slo_enforcer.hysteresis.enabled=false and rollback via the console; emergency rollback documented in docs/ops/slo-enforcer.md.

Why this is a hotfix: The incident on 2026-02-19 caused customer-facing latency spikes and some 5xxs due to repeated failovers. The change is conservative (adds hysteresis + smoothing) and low-risk.

Notes: This PR also exposes the new config knobs as runtime flags for Private/Dedicated customers; the defaults are conservative. We intend to follow up with telemetry-driven tuning (ENG-9482).
